newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First, National hold shortest meeting.
newsitem.headline: NZ First, National hold shortest meeting.

text.p: Negotiators for New Zealand First and the conservative National party on Thursday had their shortest meeting yet, but both sides continued to say the talks were going well.
"A good meeting," caretaker National Prime Minister Jim Bolger told journalists after the one and a half hour session.
He said the two parties had exchanged a number of papers.
New Zealand First Deputy Leader Tau Henare said the talks had been "very good".

NZ First leader Winston Peters and key policy analyst Peter McCardle were working on background issues and did not attend the talks. However, Henare would not comment on the issues they were addressing, nor on informal talks held between NZ First and National late on Wednesday over controversial state house rent rises.
The next round of formal talks are due next Tuesday, but the parties have said there will be other informal talks.

"They are progressing very well. We have a cordial relationship with both National and Labour. We are working to a conclusion with both parties," Henare said, adding that work on policy issues was not yet complete.
Nationalist NZ First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is negotiating with both National and the main opposition Labour party over the shape of the next government.
